title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is grappling with supply chain vulnerabilities while simultaneously pushing forward with ambitious projects. As companies pivot to microgravity testing and advanced satellite constellations, the competition for dominance in low Earth orbit continues to heat up.

themes.title: Supply Chain Woes Persist
themes.body: A recent report highlights the U.S. space sector's troubling reliance on Chinese manufacturing, raising red flags for national security. This dependency could complicate efforts to enhance domestic production capabilities.

themes.title: Microgravity Testing Gains Momentum
themes.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant has passed a critical design review, signaling progress in the race for microgravity capabilities. Meanwhile, Starfighters is gearing up its Texas facility for flight tests, indicating a renewed focus on practical applications.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion allocation for space resilience suggests a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space. This funding could bolster U.S. capabilities amid increasing global competition.

themes.title: Data Bottlenecks in LEO
themes.body: The 'cardinality wall' presents a significant challenge for data management in low Earth orbit constellations, threatening to stifle growth. As satellite networks expand, addressing this bottleneck will be crucial for operational efficiency.
